question: Can state-dependent decoding of the saved status/attribute byte identify a boss during hit and death states without pre-restore route history?
author: Lord Tom
decision: First run must reproduce F02 frame counts and defeat times, and removing the added saved_status columns must reproduce F02 trace bytes. Only then independently repeat. Full expanded traces must match. Evaluate the source-derived predicate without any search/input change; a disagreement is a falsifier, not grounds to modify the movie.
limits: External reference movie is observer qualification only; its inputs, states and routes never enter fresh search or controller learning.
FCEUX is an independent reference emulator, not QuickNES replay qualification.
Loader and attribute agreement do not by themselves establish damage or a stable enemy identity.
Only the script-advanced frames are counted exactly; any frontend setup before movie reset is additional and unmeasured.
defeat_transition: A previously live clear flag must rise in the matching boss area; power-on set bits do not count.
correction: Add one raw read per enemy slot: CPU $040C+offset. Bank07 LF536 stores prior status OR original attributes before status 6 and tag overwrite; LF4EE restores the attributes and status. Preserve every earlier field and movie setting.

hypothesis.limitations: State classification is distinct from identity continuity and new HP change across reset/restore; those require separate baseline and boundary checks.
